source.title: Formalizing Generalization and Adversarial Robustness of Neural Networks to Weight Perturbations
source.authors: Yu-Lin Tsai; Chia-Yi Hsu; Chia-Mu Yu; Pin-Yu Chen

record.tranche_reason: Tests generalization-gap behavior under adversarial weight perturbation and a proposed training loss, an extension beyond the listed versions’ settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own empirical generalization-gap results under weight PGD attacks and explicitly states how the gap changes with its regularization coefficient. Theoretical bounds and results cited from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests a proposed loss for robustness and generalization under adversarial weight perturbations, but none of V1–V8. In particular, it does not test whether magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance ranks ordinary generalization gaps among convolutional networks with similarly low training loss, as V7 specifies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: their theoretical analysis motivates a loss that improves generalization and robustness against weight perturbations in the tested settings. They also claim non-vacuous associated bounds. Appendix E demonstrates decreasing norm-based bound components alongside test error, rather than establishing numerical non-vacuity of a complete bound merely from that trend.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a custom weight-perturbation robust loss with norm regularization and adversarial weight PGD evaluation; the experiments do not implement the original sources’ methods as stated in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The empirical gap varies with the matrix norm regularization coefficient μ; the reported trend holds across the different ϵ_train values used. The gap without attack is lower when ϵ_train = 0, while its regularization trend is similar when ϵ_train ≠ 0.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing the proposed matrix norm regularization coefficient reduces the MNIST adversarial generalization gap across tested training perturbation budgets. Clean-gap experiments show a similar regularization trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed norm regularizer reduces generalization gaps in the tested weight-perturbation training setting.

fits_no_version.finding: L1 regularization reduces some measured gaps but loses accuracy or fails to converge at larger coefficients; L2 results show no consistent monotonic gap reduction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alternative weight penalties have different convergence and generalization tradeoffs in this adversarial weight-perturbation setting.

fits_no_version.finding: The study reports test accuracy under absolute, element-wise bounded weight attacks and test-error behavior as training-set size changes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-attack robustness and sample-size-dependent test error can be evaluated separately from magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of generalization gaps.

record.code_released: not stated; paper says code will be shared upon request
record.problems: The experiments use MNIST with 1000 training samples for the generalization experiment; the paper reports no random-seed error bars. Several gap results are described from figures without numerical values. The authors’ checklist says the work has no limitations, without a limitations discussion.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for detailed robustness-accuracy sweeps, quantization, runtime, and comparisons of robust loss versus naive adversarial weight training were omitted because they do not directly report the generalization-gap behavior asked about. Generalization-bound components and cited prior-work results were also omitted as they are not the measured empirical gap in the claim.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy under matched recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence and removal alongside weight decay with augmentation.

Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance as a predictor of ordinary generalization gaps among convolutional networks with similarly low training loss, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: A shared interest in weight sensitivity does not make this a V7 test. The paper explicitly distinguishes its adversarial generalization setting from standard generalization assessment. No version-specific verdicts or missing version-bearing rows are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization under standard training.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Large versus small batch generalization comparisons.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance compared across networks trained to similar training loss, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized examples and resulting test accuracy.
